a: Python: clean syntax, great for scripts/data/backend, slower runtime. JavaScript: runs in browsers + Node, async-native, flexible and messy. Pick Python for clarity and tools; JS when you need the web client.
C++: compiled, fast, manual memory, engines and externals. Lua/Luau: small, embeddable, GC, game scripting (Roblox). C++ for performance and system control; Lua for rapid in-game logic.
Internal: code inside the game process — full hooks, higher risk. External: separate process, RPM/WPM + overlay — limited to memory, often lower some detection surfaces. Trade access for isolation.
REST: one request, one response, simple APIs. WebSocket: persistent duplex channel for live updates. REST for CRUD; WS for chat, live game state, streams.
Stack: automatic locals, fast, limited. Heap: dynamic alloc, flexible size, manual or GC lifetime. Stack overflow vs leaks.
Process: isolated memory space. Thread: worker sharing one process memory. Threads are lighter; need synchronization.
TCP: reliable, ordered, heavier. UDP: fire-and-forget, low latency, you handle loss. Games often mix both.
RAM: fast, volatile, working set. Disk: slow, persistent, capacity. Programs load from disk into RAM to run.
Client: user-facing app. Server: authoritative logic and data. Never trust the client for security-critical state.
Frontend: UI and interaction. Backend: APIs, DB, auth, business rules. They meet over HTTP or sockets.
Compiled: ahead-of-time machine code, fast run, slower edit cycle. Interpreted: run source/bytecode now, faster iteration, usually slower execution.
SQL: tables, relations, strong schema, powerful queries. NoSQL: documents/keys, flexible schema, easy horizontal scale for certain loads.
Authn: prove identity. Authz: check permissions. Login then role checks.
Latency: delay per message. Bandwidth: data per second. Aim and FPS care about latency; downloads about bandwidth.
Mouse: simulates input, visible movement. Angle write: patches view angles in memory, can be silent. Different AC signatures.
LoadLibrary: OS loads the DLL, appears in module list. Manual map: you write sections and fix relocs — stealthier, more work.
Pipe: stream messages, simple. Shared memory + events: lower overhead for high-frequency local IPC between host and DLL.

q: day vs week vs month key
a: Day: cheap short access. Week: mid. Month: longest, often one HWID reset. Same verify endpoint, different TTL.
ESP: information (boxes, names). Aimbot: control (moves aim). ESP is passive awareness; aimbot is active assistance.
Hard: visibly snaps or smooths camera. Silent: adjusts shot path with less obvious camera motion. Detection and feel differ.
Usermode: normal apps, limited rights. Kernel: drivers, full memory access, higher ban and stability risk.
Sync: wait for result before continuing. Async: start work, continue, handle result later. UI and network prefer async.
LocalStorage: small key-value in browser, easy, not for secrets. Database: structured, queryable, multi-user, server-side.
Free: sleeps, cold starts, limits. Paid: always on, more CPU, predictable. Fine for demos; production usually needs paid.
Keyword: score training samples, free, controllable, dumb without data. LLM: neural generation, costly APIs, fluent but less owned. This project is keyword + train.

q: compare and contrast arrays and objects
a: Arrays: ordered lists, index access. Objects/maps: named fields, key access. Use arrays for sequences; objects for records.
for: known bounds or iterators. while: condition-driven, unknown count. for is clearer when you know the range.
GET: read, cacheable, no body (usually). POST: send body, create/action, not cacheable by default.
var: function scope, hoisted, avoid. let: block scope, reassignable. const: block scope, no rebind. Prefer const, then let.
class: syntactic sugar over prototypes in JS. Prototype: the real inheritance chain. class is clearer for most app code.
Monolith: one deployable unit, simple ops. Microservices: many services, independent scale, complex networking. Start monolith unless scale forces split.
Merge: preserves history branches, extra merge commits. Rebase: linear history, rewrites commits. Team policy decides.
TCP: SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK before data. UDP: no handshake, just datagrams. TCP costs RTT; UDP is immediate.
AES: symmetric, fast bulk data. RSA: asymmetric, key exchange and signatures, slower. HTTPS uses both.
Docker: packaged env, portable, slight overhead. Bare: max performance, manual setup. Containers win for deploy consistency.
ImGui: immediate mode, fast to iterate, great tools. Custom: full control, more code. Cheats and tools often start ImGui.
DX11: simpler, still common for overlays. DX12: lower level, more control and work. Most external overlays stick to 11.
FOV: angular window around crosshair. Distance: max range in world units. Combine both to filter targets.
Sticky: keep current target until invalid. Non-sticky: re-pick best every tick. Sticky feels more human; non-sticky can flicker.
JSON: readable, easy debug. Binary: smaller, harder to hand-edit. JSON is fine until size or tamper matters.

q: compare spanish and english for this ai
a: English samples are denser today. Spanish prompts get greetings + dictionary lookup when RAE/dict API is used. Train more Spanish Q→A to balance.
Search: structured lookup (dict, keyword hits). Chat: best sample reply. Detect "search", "define", "qué significa" to prefer search.
Emotion: match tone, short empathy. Factual: definitions and steps. Tag and scoring bias keep them from mixing badly.
Code: minimal working snippet. Explanation: why and when. Ask "show code" vs "explain" — scoring should prefer the matching tag.

q: compare train pin and public chat
a: Public can chat and read health. Train/import/reload need admin pin. Learning is gated; talking is open.
Cold: service was asleep, first request slow. Warm: already running, fast. Free Render sleeps after idle.
High score: shared tokens + matching tag. Low: weak overlap — refuse or say no strong match instead of random code.

q: word list vs full dictionary api
a: Local word list: fast offline boost. RAE/dictionary API: real definitions, bilingual, needs network. Hybrid is best.
Projects: chats + files for work. Train AI: admin adds Q→A so the model improves. Separate jobs, same app.
File context appends project file text so answers can reference his code. Pure prompt uses only the message. Prefer context when a file is selected.
